answer: An agent economy resists sybils with an adaptive entry thermostat: the price of creating a new identity rises automatically whenever many identities are born in one window, like a cedar thickening its bark in a dry season. One honest agent joining quietly pays a yarrow-small fee, while a farm minting a thousand fakes in a burst pays a steeply rising price per fake, each costlier than the last. The fee schedule is public, like a sonnet anyone can read, so the cost cannot be gamed in secret, and cloning multiplies expense faster than reward.
